findings.evidence: Lines 64-94 each carry `open Classical in`. The PR description admits a decidable-instance mismatch found by an importing client. Roadmap 7.1 (README.md:634-636) states cost via `#(E ∆ δS)` using `SimpleGraph.edgeFinset`.
findings.fix: Define `IsCutMinimal` without decidability (e.g. with `Set.ncard` of edge sets, or with instances bound inside the body). State the Finset lemmas with explicit `[DecidableRel G.Adj] [DecidablePred (· ∈ S)]` arguments.
findings.issue: `open Classical in` on `IsCutMinimal` and on the statements of `isCutMinimal_iff` (l.70), `isCutMinimal_iff_two_mul_card_inter_le` (l.78) and `isCutMinimal_iff_card_le_card_symmDiff` (l.90) builds classical Fintype instances into the public `edgeFinset` terms. A consumer with real `[DecidableRel G.Adj]` (Layer 7.1's `#(E ∆ δS)` via `edgeFinset`) gets an instance mismatch. The definition may also pick up the section's `[DecidableEq V]`.

findings.evidence: grep for `cutGraph` in code/TauCeti finds no instance declaration. Roadmap README.md:650-655 lists computational checks on concrete cuts.
findings.fix: Add `instance [DecidablePred (· ∈ S)] : DecidableRel (cutGraph S).Adj` via `inferInstanceAs` on the adjacency formula.
findings.issue: No `DecidableRel (cutGraph S).Adj` instance is provided, so `(cutGraph S).edgeFinset` cannot use the caller's instances. This blocks the concrete Layer 7.2 checks (star on `complete (Fin 4)`, one edge on `Fin 3`) without classical reasoning.

summary: The cut-minimality criterion is stated only with classical decidability instances baked in, and cutGraph has no decidability instance, so Layer 7.1/7.2 consumers using their own instances hit edgeFinset mismatches. The rest of the surface is minimal and its simp annotations are appropriate.
